sources.title: Solari Papers
sources.passageSummary: Four papers are listed, dated August 2023 to January 2025; individual paper bodies are not all read.

sources.title: Missing Money 2020 Update
sources.publisher: Mark Skidmore and Catherine Austin Fitts
sources.sourceLocator: Introduction and Uses, paragraphs before/after top-ten table
sources.passageSummary: Authors discuss 170 unsupported year-end adjustments totaling $2.1 trillion within the FY2015 $6.5 trillion set. They present unrecognized spending/debt as possibilities and explicitly call the debt work preliminary.
sources.independenceRoot: Mark Skidmore and Catherine Austin Fitts

sources.title: DoD and HUD Missing Money Supporting Documentation
sources.passageSummary: A curated route to underlying reports; no blanket read or authentication of every linked report.

sources.title: Army General Fund Adjustments Not Adequately Documented or Supported, DODIG-2016-113
sources.passageSummary: The official indexed summary reports $2.8 trillion third-quarter and $6.5 trillion year-end adjustments and says these amounts are not cumulative. The direct page and official PDF returned 403.

sources.title: SFFAS 56: Classified Activities, Handbook Version 24
sources.sourceLocator: Handbook pages 5–6, paragraphs 11–14; page 10, A10; 9/25 handbook edition
sources.passageSummary: The standard permits specified modifications to prevent classified-information disclosure and prescribes general disclosures. The text is not a record of a particular payment or program.

sources.title: Interview 1497 — Catherine Austin Fitts on Where the Missing Trillions Are Going
sources.sourceLocator: Transcript opening, speaker-labeled Fitts and Corbett turns through SFFAS56 discussion
sources.passageSummary: Fitts describes an expensive global national-security system and interprets accounting secrecy as obscuring financial reality. These are her attributed positions; Corbett’s framing remains his own.

sources.title: Empire Endgame: Digital Slave Population!
sources.passageSummary: Publisher identifies Liszt interviewing Fitts and summarizes themes of secrecy, debt and technological control. No verbatim guest statement is inferred from this synopsis.

sources.title: 2nd Quarter 2026 Wrap Up: News Trends & Stories, Part II with Dr. Joseph P. Farrell
sources.sourceLocator: Title, dated summary and subscriber gate
sources.passageSummary: Public summary names Fitts and Farrell discussing quarterly stories; the subscriber program and audio were not accessed.

sources.title: The Solari Papers #3: Musings on the Department of Defense
sources.sourceLocator: Byline and introductory paragraphs; continuation/PDF linked
sources.passageSummary: Fitts frames the paper as connecting her encounters with defense activity to financial and governance questions. Only the displayed introduction was inspected.

sources.title: Archived Events
sources.sourceLocator: 2017 entry: April 27 interview, June 20 public availability
sources.passageSummary: Index distinguishes the Empire Endgame interview date from its public availability date; it is the same episode lineage as SOL-S07, not independent corroboration.

sources.title: A Correspondence
sources.passageSummary: Search discovery mentions Farrell forwarding correspondence. Full body unavailable; no historical edge promoted.

sources.passageSummary: Uninspected lead retained for later recovery.

claims.proposition: Skidmore and Fitts frame additional unrecognized spending or debt as possibilities for further inquiry, not a completed measurement of stolen cash.
In the publisher transcript, Fitts interprets financial secrecy through her national-security-system model; this records her position, not an independently traced destination of funds.
The publisher identifies a Liszt–Fitts interview dated April 27, 2017; Solari separately lists June 20 public availability.
The public Solari summary identifies Fitts and Farrell as participants in its July 28, 2026 quarterly discussion.
SFFAS56 contains classified-reporting modification rules; attribution of specific spending requires further records.
